sections.h2: Which Franklin County, Illinois offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Franklin County runs property tax out of the Government Annex Building at 901 Public Square in Benton, the county seat. One phone number, 618-435-9800, reaches the Treasurer, the Supervisor of Assessments and the Board of Review, and the offices keep weekday hours from eight in the morning to four in the afternoon.

  • Treasurer: collects the bill, takes mail at PO Box 967, Benton, IL 62812, and runs the delinquent tax sale
  • Supervisor of Assessments: serves as chief county assessment officer, handles exemptions and mailing address changes
  • Board of Review: three county citizens appointed by the County Board, with the chief assessment officer acting as clerk
  • County Clerk: the place to learn how to pay delinquent taxes after a sale

Township assessors set the starting values. The county lists assessors for Goode/Barren, Benton, Browning, Cave/Eastern, Denning, Ewing/Northern, Frankfort, Six Mile and Tyrone, so call the assessment office to learn who covers your parcel.

sections.h2: How is a Franklin County property tax bill calculated?
sections.html:
Two numbers drive it: the value your township assessor gives the property, and the money your local taxing districts say they need for the coming year. The assessment office compares the process to income tax, where a rate is applied to a base.

About 60% of the property tax collected goes to education, and the rest is shared among the county, cities, park districts, library districts, fire districts, townships and other special districts. The treasurer's page says money is spread across more than fifty local governments, and the largest share goes to the school district where the property sits.

Rates are part of the puzzle too. Assessments can fall while rates climb, because a rate depends on the total levy and the total equalized assessed value in the district. A rate report for 2025 taxes payable in 2026 is posted on the Treasurer's page, and your own bill shows the rate for your taxing districts.

Properties inside a tax increment finance district work differently. Taxes on growth above the "TIF Base" go to the TIF fund instead of the other taxing bodies. The Treasurer gives the formula as (Net Taxable Value minus TIF Base) times the Tax Rate, and notes that the county does not create TIF districts or control how the money is spent.

sections.h2: What are the late penalties and tax sale rules in Franklin County?
sections.html:
Illinois law requires the county collector to add a 1.5% penalty for each month an installment is late, and an installment counts as timely only when paid on or before its due date. Unpaid tax is sold at the annual tax sale.

Franklin County tax and appeal rules (source: Franklin County Treasurer and Board of Review)
RuleWhat the county page says
Late payment penalty1.5% per month on each late installment
Tax buyer interest, first yearInitial maximum rate of 18%
Tax buyer interest, later yearsInitial rate of 12% on subsequent years' taxes the buyer pays
Board of Review startConvenes the first Monday in June
Complaint window30 calendar days after the assessment list is published
Evidence for unequal treatment5 comparable properties with size, age and condition

At the sale, bidders pay the taxes and penalties and then charge the owner interest. If the owner does not repay the buyer within the allowed time, the buyer may ask a court for a deed to the property. The county also takes sealed bids on real estate and mobile homes it has acquired for delinquent taxes, and a delinquent tax agent runs a yearly sale of those parcels.

sections.h2: Where can a Franklin County owner contest an assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the township assessor or the Board of Review, since each has its own time frame. The Board takes complaints in writing on its own forms, signed and showing the address of the property, within 30 calendar days after the assessment list is published for the year at issue.

All evidence must go in with the original complaint, because the Board looks only at what it receives. An overvaluation complaint needs proof such as an appraisal. A complaint about unequal treatment needs five comparable properties in your area with square footage, age and condition for each.

If you are unhappy with the Board's ruling, the next stop is the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board. The Treasurer adds that a taxpayer who still has a dispute after the complaint process can go to circuit court, but must keep paying the billed tax meanwhile to avoid tax liens. Keep a copy of whatever you file as proof.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can Franklin County homeowners claim?
sections.html:
Most exemptions require the home to be residential, owned and lived in by the taxpayer. The Supervisor of Assessments lists these programs:

  • General homestead exemption for owner-occupied single-family homes
  • Senior citizens homestead exemption for owners 65 and older
  • Senior assessment freeze, which needs Form PTAX-340 filed every year
  • Homestead improvement exemption, which covers four years after an improvement is finished and occupied
  • Disabled persons exemption, filed on PTAX-343 and renewed each year with PTAX-343-R
  • Disabled veterans standard and disabled veterans homestead exemptions
  • Returning veterans exemption, on Form PTAX-341

The dollar amounts change almost every year, so ask the assessment office for current figures. Only the general homestead and senior homestead exemptions skip annual renewal. Seniors can also use the county's real estate tax deferral through the Treasurer, which puts a lien on the home and is repaid when it sells or transfers, and the state's Circuit Breaker grant is applied for with the Illinois Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: What should sellers know about Franklin County itself?
sections.html:
Franklin County is in Southern Illinois, in the region called Little Egypt. It was created on January 2, 1818, from parts of Gallatin and White counties, and Benton is the seat while West Frankfort is the largest city. The county holds 409 square miles of land plus a good deal of water, including the Wayne Fitzgerrell State Recreation Area.

Coal shaped the county. Mining began in 1889 at the King Coal Mine, and the county saw eleven mine disasters between 1905 and 1968. The Tri-State Tornado of March 18, 1925 struck West Frankfort and killed 192 people in the county.

Census QuickFacts counts 36,916 residents in 2025, down 2.3% from the 2020 base, and 18,461 housing units. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $89,000 for 2020 through 2024, 74.1% of housing units are owner-occupied, and median household income is $56,740. Median gross rent is $803 and 16.4% of residents live in poverty. Only 19 building permits were issued in 2025.

Public school districts include Benton Community Consolidated District 47, Christopher Unit District 99, Frankfort Community Unit District 168, Sesser-Valier Unit District 196, Zeigler-Royalton Unit District 188 and Ewing-Northern Community Consolidated District 115.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work when a Franklin County house sells?
sections.html:
The tax bill is mailed to the owner at the address on the deed. According to the Treasurer, in typical transactions the seller compensates the buyer for real estate taxes at closing, and the two sides negotiate that point between them.

Call the Treasurer for the installment dates and the amount still owed on the parcel, since the bill itself carries the exact figures. A house with unpaid taxes can be in line for the tax sale, so a seller who is behind should clear it up before the sale date. To change the address where the bill goes, return the county's change of address form to the Supervisor of Assessments.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Franklin County, Illinois?
faqs.a: Pay the Franklin County Treasurer at the Government Annex Building, 901 Public Square in Benton, or by mail to PO Box 967. The office phone is 618-435-9800. The county also posts a real estate tax inquiry link on its website.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty for Franklin County property tax?
faqs.a: The penalty is 1.5% per month on each late installment, as required by Illinois law. An installment is on time only if it is paid by its due date. Unpaid tax can be sold at the annual tax sale.

faqs.q: How fast can a Franklin County tax buyer charge interest?
faqs.a: A winning bidder at the tax sale charges the owner interest at an initial maximum rate of 18%. If the tax buyer pays later years' taxes too, the initial rate on those is 12%.

faqs.q: Who hears assessment complaints in Franklin County?
faqs.a: The Board of Review hears them. It has three citizen members appointed by the County Board, and complaints are due within 30 calendar days after the assessment list is published. Appeals from the Board go to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Franklin County house if the tax is unpaid?
faqs.a: The county's pages say buyer and seller negotiate the tax at closing, and they do not bar a sale. Phone the Treasurer for the exact balance first, so the closing statement carries the right figure.
